head_commit.message:
ci: fix macOS WPT (Python 3.15) and job timeout on v7.x

The macOS runner image now ships Python 3.15, which removed
node:http's CGIHTTPRequestHandler. pywebsocket3, used by the WPT server,
still needs it, so 'wpt serve' crashes on macOS and the test:wpt step hangs
until the job times out. Pin Python to 3.14 on macOS (via actions/setup-python,
matching main) so the WPT server starts.

Also give the test job a flat 30-minute timeout (matching main) instead of 20,
so the macOS matrix has enough time to complete the full suite.

head_commit.message:
fix(h2): replay requests whose HEADERS raced a GOAWAY (#6065)

* fix(h2): replay requests whose HEADERS raced a GOAWAY

A stream opened before the client processes a GOAWAY but flushed after it is
refused by nghttp2 and surfaces as a frameError on the HEADERS frame. When the
GOAWAY's lastStreamID covers the stream (2^31-1, the graceful shutdown notice
hyper, Go and nghttp2 send), the request stays attached to the session and the
frameError rejected it, although the peer never saw it.

Requeue such requests when the body is replayable, within the GOAWAY replay
budget.

Refs: https://github.com/nodejs/undici/issues/6064

head_commit.message:
fix(fetch): preserve abort propagation after garbage collection

Copied and cloned requests can lose cancellation after garbage collection
because their signals do not keep forwarding controllers alive.

Native AbortSignal composition can retain finalization records while a
long-lived source survives on supported Node.js versions.

For 5,000 constructor copies of one retained parent, Node 24.20.0 / V8
13.6.233.17-node.53 improves from 35.37 us to 0.83 us per copy.
Two fresh processes use 50,000 warm-up operations and seven trials,
discarding the fastest and slowest.

Fixes: https://github.com/nodejs/undici/issues/4068
Refs: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/62363
Signed-off-by: Ruben Bridgewater <ruben.bridgewater@datadoghq.com>

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(http2): keep persistent error sink on released streams (#5983)

head_commit.message:
fix(http2): keep persistent error sink on released streams (#5983)

* fix(http2): keep persistent error sink on released streams

When an HTTP/2 session is torn down with an error (e.g. the idle reaper
in onHttp2SessionIdleTimeout), Node fans that error out to every native
stream still tracked in the session's internal state. A released stream
that no longer has an 'error' listener then crashes the process with an
unhandled `InformationalError: socket idle timeout` (#5936).

releaseRequestStream, severRequestStream and releaseUpgradeStream only
installed a one-shot `once('error', noop)` sink (and not at all in
onError), so a single late error consumed it and the subsequent
session-level error went unhandled.

Keep a persistent `on('error', noop)` sink on every stream undici stops
tracking, and add a noop fallback in onError when the real handler is
removed. Retain the sink on upgrade streams instead of dropping it in
onUpgradeStreamClose.

Closes #5936.

* test(http2): make idle reaper regression test cross-platform robust

The released stream is only observable in the window between its 'end' and
'close' events. On some platforms (Node 25/macOS) that window is too short to
inspect, so the previous synchronous assertion failed CI. Poll briefly for the
released stream and skip the test when the teardown race cannot be observed,
instead of failing. The test still fails on the buggy implementation whenever
the window is observable.

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(cache): ignore SQLITE_BUSY in the sqlite cache store (#6049)

head_commit.message:
fix(cache): ignore SQLITE_BUSY in the sqlite cache store (#6049)

The store is meant to be shared between processes. SQLite reports a
database another connection is writing as SQLITE_BUSY/SQLITE_LOCKED
("database is locked"), and those errors currently propagate out of
get(), set(), delete() and the pruning that set() performs, failing the
request that triggered the write.

Caching is best effort, so skip the operation instead of throwing: a
locked database is a cache miss, and the next request retries.

Co-authored-by: AdityaProCoder <83160620+AdityaProCoder@users.noreply.github.com>

head_commit.message:
docs: clarify that `origin` is optional only for origin-bound dispatchers (#5994)

Fixes #1011.

`Dispatcher.md` documented the `origin` option of `dispatcher.dispatch()` as
"(optional)", which reads as "never required". That only holds for a dispatcher
already bound to a single origin. `Agent` is not bound to one origin and
requires it.

Verified against current `main`:

  new Pool(origin).request({ path, method })   -> 200
  new Client(origin).request({ path, method })  -> 200
  new Agent().request({ path, method })         -> InvalidArgumentError
                                                'opts.origin must be a
                                                 non-empty string or URL.'
  new Agent().request({ origin, path, method }) -> 200

`Client`/`Pool` fill the origin from `this[kUrl].origin` when `kDispatch` builds
the Request (lib/dispatcher/client.js), while `Agent` rejects a missing origin
in its own `dispatch` (lib/dispatcher/agent.js). `docs/docs/api/Agent.md` already
calls `origin` "Required." for `Agent.dispatch()`; this aligns the abstract
Dispatcher docs with it.

Adds test/node-test/dispatcher-optional-origin.js to pin the distinction, which

head_commit.message:
fix(h2): give the liveness probe a minimum deadline

Stream timeouts can be tens of milliseconds, shorter than an event-loop
stall on a healthy process; a probe bounded only by that timeout could
tear down a live connection. Wait at least one second for the PING ack.

leaves open at teardown: the probe PING can still be in flight when the
client closes, which on Windows turns the close into a reset that
surfaced as an uncaught ECONNRESET.

head_commit.message:
fix(cache): ignore SQLITE_BUSY in the sqlite cache store

The store is meant to be shared between processes. SQLite reports a
database another connection is writing as SQLITE_BUSY/SQLITE_LOCKED
("database is locked"), and those errors currently propagate out of
get(), set(), delete() and the pruning that set() performs, failing the
request that triggered the write.

Caching is best effort, so skip the operation instead of throwing: a
locked database is a cache miss, and the next request retries.

head_commit.message:
fix(cookies): ignore a numeric expires outside the Date range (#5832)

stringify guarded expires with a string comparison that only works for the
Date form:

    if (cookie.expires != null && cookie.expires.toString() !== 'Invalid Date')

A Date whose time value is NaN stringifies to "Invalid Date" and is skipped,
but a number never does: NaN.toString() is "NaN" and 1e16.toString() is
"10000000000000000". The guard therefore always passes for a number outside
the range representable by Date, and toIMFDate reads NaN/undefined from every
getter and splices those tokens into the header value:

    setCookie(headers, { name: 'Space', value: 'Cat', expires: 1e16 })
    // Space=Cat; Expires=undefined, undefined undefined NaN undefined:undefined:undefined GMT

The emitted value is not a valid IMF-fixdate. The Max-Age branch a few lines
above already tests the type rather than a stringified value.

Treat a number as absent only when it is not a valid time value, keeping the
existing Date behaviour. Name the upper bound so it is clear it is the largest
time value a Date can represent rather than a magic number.

Non-finite numbers reach stringify already coerced to 0 by the unsigned long
long converter in lib/web/cookies/index.js, so they keep serializing as the
epoch; that coercion is a separate concern.

head_commit.message:
fix(websocket,eventsource): keep receive limits behind dispatcher wrappers (#5896)

* fix(websocket): keep receive limits behind dispatcher wrappers

WebSocket and WebSocketStream read maxPayloadSize and maxFragments from
the dispatcher's webSocketOptions, which only DispatcherBase provides.
For any other dispatcher the parser got undefined and treated it as 0,
i.e. no limit. That covered RetryAgent, MockAgent/SnapshotAgent,
Dispatcher1Wrapper and custom dispatchers, including when one of them is
set as the global dispatcher. A configured limit was ignored, and even
the 128 MB default was lost, so a ~128 KB compressed frame could inflate
to an unbounded message.

- The parser falls back to the documented defaults (131072 fragments,
  128 MB) when no value is provided, and passes the resolved limit to
  permessage-deflate. An explicit 0 still disables a limit.
- The defaults live in lib/core/constants.js, shared with DispatcherBase.
- RetryAgent, MockAgent and Dispatcher1Wrapper report the wrapped
  dispatcher's webSocketOptions.

EventSource reads maxEventSize from the dispatcher's eventSourceOptions,
which only DispatcherBase provides. Behind RetryAgent, MockAgent/
SnapshotAgent or Dispatcher1Wrapper the configured limit was ignored and
the default (buffer.kStringMaxLength) applied instead.

Forward eventSourceOptions to the wrapped dispatcher, as is now done for
webSocketOptions.

head_commit.message:
test(http2): make idle reaper regression test cross-platform robust

The released stream is only observable in the window between its 'end' and

inspect, so the previous synchronous assertion failed CI. Poll briefly for the
released stream and skip the test when the teardown race cannot be observed,
instead of failing. The test still fails on the buggy implementation whenever
the window is observable.

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(deduplicate): detach the primary on abort instead of rejecting the group

head_commit.message:
fix(deduplicate): detach the primary on abort instead of rejecting the group

Aborting the first request of a coalesced group cancelled the shared
dispatch, so every other caller waiting on it — including callers that
passed no signal — was rejected with an AbortError. Coalescing was not
transparent: whether your request succeeded depended on who asked first
and whether they had a timeout.

Hand the primary a proxied controller (same shape as the waiting
handlers). Aborting it now settles only the primary and detaches it from
the group; the underlying request is cancelled only once no member —
primary or waiting handler — is left waiting. This also releases the
pendingRequests entry when every member of a group aborts, so a later
request never joins a group with no consumers left. With no waiters the
abort still propagates exactly as before.

Refs: https://github.com/nodejs/undici/issues/5711
Signed-off-by: Paco Cartones <pacocartones@users.noreply.github.com>

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(mock): guard aborted requests in async reply callback rejection

head_commit.message:
fix(mock): guard aborted requests in async reply callback rejection

When a reply options callback returns a promise, the request can be
aborted while that promise is still pending. controller.abort() then
settles the request through onResponseError. If the callback promise
later rejects, the rejection arm called handler.onResponseError(null,
err) again, double-settling an already-aborted request.

Add the same `if (aborted) return` guard that handleReply() already uses
so the late rejection is dropped once the request has been aborted.

Signed-off-by: Paco Cartones <pacocartones@users.noreply.github.com>

head_commit.message:
test(mock): make the delayed-abort test discriminate instead of asserting true

The first case in test/mock-delayed-abort.js ended with p.ok(true, 'No
uncaught errors after delayed response'), a tautology: the bare MockAgent
path throws no uncaught error when a delayed reply is delivered on top of
an abort, so the assertion stayed green even against code that dropped the
post-abort guards. Verified by reverting the aborted-guards in
lib/mock/mock-utils.js — only the composed-interceptor and DecoratorHandler
cases failed; this one still passed.

Wrap the dispatch handler in a DecoratorHandler that records any
onResponseStart/onResponseData/onResponseEnd delivered after onResponseError
and assert none occur. It now fails against the reverted guards and passes
against real code, covering the full response side of the contract for the
bare-agent path (the sibling test asserts only onResponseStart).

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(mock): settle the dispatch when an async reply data function rejects

head_commit.message:
fix(mock): settle request when reply data function rejects

The data-function form of .reply(statusCode, data) already awaits a
returned promise and re-runs handleReply with the resolved body, but the
promise had no rejection handler. When the data function rejects, no
terminal onResponse* callback fires: the dispatched request never settles
(hang) and the rejection surfaces as an unhandledRejection.

Add a rejection arm that mirrors the reply-options-callback path: respect
an in-flight abort, then delete the mock dispatch and emit a single
onResponseError on the controller.

Signed-off-by: Paco Cartones <pacocartones@users.noreply.github.com>

workflow_runs.display_title: fix(websocket): remove WebSocketStream handshake abort listener after the handshake

head_commit.message:
fix(websocket): remove WebSocketStream handshake abort listener

A WebSocketStream created with a signal added an abort listener during the

opening handshake but never removed it. After the connection was

established (or closed) the listener became a no-op yet stayed attached to

the signal, so a long-lived signal kept every closed WebSocketStream and

its listener closure alive, leaking memory and eventually triggering a

MaxListenersExceededWarning when a signal is reused across streams.

Remove the listener once the handshake concludes (on established, on

socket close, and after the abort steps run).

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 4.8
Signed-off-by: Paco Cartones <pacocartones@users.noreply.github.com>

head_commit.message:
fix(pool): keep caller async context for queued requests

Requests waiting in the Pool queue were dispatched from whichever
callback drained it (another request's connect or drain), so
Client#dispatch and the undici:request:create diagnostics channel ran
in the wrong AsyncLocalStorage context. Since #5799 every concurrent
HTTPS request is queued during ALPN negotiation, which made this hit
fetch() by default.

Capture the caller's async context when queueing and dispatch inside it.

Fixes: #5981

* chore: drop stale milo entries from .npmignore

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Xf8iHe9HroHgZuP6UXGZnx
Signed-off-by: Matteo Collina <hello@matteocollina.com>

* fix(cache): always treat zero-lifetime entries as stale

Responses stored with a zero freshness lifetime (e.g. max-age=0 with an
etag) get staleAt === cachedAt. isStale() used `now > staleAt`, so a
reuse in the same millisecond as the store (or after the clock stepped
back) served the entry as fresh without revalidation. This made
'stores response with max-age=0 and etag, revalidates it on reuse'
flaky on CI.
